newsitem.title: USA: New Jersey to freeze some local property taxes.
newsitem.headline: New Jersey to freeze some local property taxes.

text.p: - The New Jersey Assembly passed a bill Thursday to freeze low- and middle-income senior citizens' property taxes imposed by local governments.
Localities would not lose income. The state would pay for any increases.
The bill now heads to the state Senate.

The plan would fix property tax liability at 1997 rates for those persons over 65 or who are disabled, and whose income is no more than $17,550, or $21,519 for married couples. Starting next year, the state would repay them for any tax increases imposed by local governments or school districts.
The nonpartisan Office of Legislative Services puts the statewide average rise in property taxes at $152.

Assembly Speaker Jack Collins, the sponsor, estimated the cost to the treasury next year would be $18.4 million to cover claims from the 140,000 eligible taxpayers. But the cost will increase rapidly -- rising to $52 million in three years and $140 million in a decade, he said.
